answer: design target: one plant over amber in the winter quarters of 2027 and no other (final wording at ship from the generator)
answer_source: the design note's Ladder; at ship task180/golden/, written by the generator from target/ and recomputed by the verifier

world.org_type: state geological survey's seismological service, running the induced-seismicity networks around deep geothermal district-heating plants

driver: An event enters the record only when it rises above the noise at the instruments, and where that noise follows a daily cycle the smallest events are recorded only in the quiet hours, so a unit's record understates its small events by the share of the day they are masked while its size distribution still passes the usual completeness tests; when a forward change removes the masking, the unit's count rises to its true rate, which only its quiet-hour record or its fully recorded sizes reveal.
driver_concrete: The survey's surface stations around one plant stand in town, where traffic and industry noise through the working day hides most earthquakes below ML 1.8, so that plant's 2026 catalogue holds its small events mainly from the night hours and still looks complete near ML 0.7 on the maximum-curvature test; the borehole stations required from January 2027 locate every ML 0.6 event at any hour, so its 2027 count rises to its true rate, over amber in the winter quarters, while every rural plant's catalogue is already complete and stays under.
stump: A competent solver counts each plant's 2026 earthquakes of ML 1.0 or more within 5 km of its injection well from the reviewed catalogue, quarter by quarter, carries them into 2027 on the unchanged injection plans and finds no plant over amber; the step that lands it there is reading the 2026 catalogue as complete at ML 1.0 when the town stations around one plant lose most daytime events below ML 1.8, so that plant's true rate, recovered from its night hours or from its magnitudes above 1.8, puts it over amber in the winter quarters once the borehole network records it.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads the counting rule and the reviewed catalogue correctly counts each plant's 2026 events of ML 1.0 or more within 5 km per quarter, confirms completeness with the maximum-curvature test (about ML 0.7 at every plant), carries the counts into 2027 and files that no plant goes over amber; it is wrong because one plant's completeness changes with the hour of the day.
domain_test: The deciding analysis is the seismologist's assessment of catalogue completeness by place and time of day and the Gutenberg-Richter rate it supports; with another field's nouns there is no magnitude-frequency law, no detection threshold set by ambient ground noise and nothing to recover from the quiet hours.
layer1: origin times in UTC against a counting rule in local calendar quarters across the daylight-saving changes
a preliminary catalogue (the one the quarterly reports were counted on) superseded by the reviewed catalogue, with relocations, magnitude revisions and explosions reclassified at review
the national agency's catalogue duplicating the larger events under its own ids and moment magnitudes
quarry blasts in the working day near two plants
station outages and a sensor swap that changes a station code
operators' injection reports in m3 with corrected resubmissions

differentiation.task228: task228 estimates sensor error from triple collocation with a shared input; task180's decisive quantity is a detection completeness that varies with the hour of the day, recovered from the quiet hours, with no collocated instruments
differentiation.task230: task230's hit rate falls as targets grow rarer at a fixed detector; task180's detector loses small events on a daily noise cycle at one site, and the forward change is the removal of that masking
differentiation.task181: task181 forecasts losses of separation from crossing pairs of aircraft; task180 forecasts located earthquakes once incomplete daytime detection ends, with no interaction or exposure construction
differentiation.task229: task229's counter captures a smaller share as the arrival rate rises, so a new signal that packs arrivals into its green phase cuts capture below the average-rate curve (a convex capture function evaluated at the wrong rate); task180's network loses small earthquakes on a daily ambient-noise cycle that does not depend on the event rate, its record still passes the standard completeness test, and the forward change removes the masking, so the true rate is recovered from the quiet hours

lineage.driver: A suspected effect of starting a treatment is tested by comparing the people who start it with people who do not, but the people who start it are chosen for a reason that already carries the outcome, a trait no recorded variable captures, so the comparison, adjusted for everything recorded, names the treatment its users were already at risk under; only comparing each person's outcomes in the window just after starting with the same person's other time, which cancels every fixed trait, finds the treatment that changes the outcome.

notes: Re-root of task180 to architecture 4, drawn 2026-10-12. Anomaly Detection & Diagnostics: the anomaly is a plant whose seismicity will run over the traffic-light system's amber in 2027; the diagnosis is that its quiet 2026 record is an artifact of daytime noise at its town stations. The counting rule and the 2027 network's design completeness are filed literally; the forecast's method is open and forced by the record (small events at that plant arrive by night at the rate the other plants show around the clock). Stump strategy 'other': the decisive structure is the observation process itself, a detection completeness that changes with the hour of the day at one site (selection into the record by ambient noise), which none of the listed strategies names; the nearest are population_selection (who is in the record) and time_semantics (local hours), neither of which is the move.
